chapters.title: Chapter 3: Form 26AS, Your Tax Credit Statement

lessons.title: Reading Form 26AS Part by Part: TDS, TCS, Advance Tax and Refunds

children.text: Priya has downloaded her Form 26AS for AY 2026-27. It runs to ten numbered parts, and most of them say "No Transactions Present". That is normal. For a typical salaried taxpayer, only two or three parts carry any data. The skill is knowing which part to look at for which question, and what the columns are telling you.

body.text: Every entry in Form 26AS is money already paid to the government on your behalf. If it is there and you do not claim it, you pay tax twice.

children.text: The Ten Parts at a Glance
Since AY 2023-24, Form 26AS has been organised into Parts I to X. Here is what each one holds and when it is likely to matter to you.

cells: You earn salary, FD interest, dividends, professional fees or commission
TDS details where Form 15G or 15H was submitted
You gave a bank a declaration asking it not to deduct TDS
Transactions under the provisos to sections 194B, 194R and 194S
You won a prize in kind or received benefits or crypto paid in kind
TDS u/s 194IA, 194IB, 194M and 194S, for the seller, landlord, contractor or professional
You sold property, received high rent, or received large fees from individuals
Virtual digital asset transactions reported in Form 26QE, for the seller
You sold crypto to an individual buyer
You made a large foreign remittance, bought an overseas tour package, or a car above ₹10 lakh
You received an income tax refund during the year
TDS u/s 194IA, 194IB, 194M and 194S, for the buyer, tenant or payer
You bought property, paid high rent, or paid large contractor fees and deducted TDS yourself
Virtual digital asset transactions reported in Form 26QE, for the buyer
You bought crypto from an individual and deducted TDS
TDS and TCS defaults found on processing statements
You filed a TDS statement yourself, such as for a property purchase, and it had errors or delays

body.text: Parts IV and VIII describe the same kinds of transaction from opposite sides. If you sell a flat, the buyer's TDS shows in your Part IV as a credit. The buyer sees the same deduction in their Part VIII as a record of what they deducted, not as a credit.

children.text: Part I: Where Most of Your Credit Lives

Part I lists every deductor who reported TDS against your PAN, one summary row each: the deductor's name and TAN, the total amount paid or credited to you, the total tax deducted and the total TDS deposited. Expand a row and you see each transaction separately, with the section code, transaction date, booking status, date of booking and amounts.

body.caption: Priya's Form 26AS Part I, AY 2026-27 (TANs illustrative)

children.text: Notice what is not here: her ₹38,000 of SBI interest and ₹6,000 HDFC Bank dividend. No TDS was deducted on either, so neither appears in Form 26AS. Both show up in AIS, which Chapter 4 covers.
Reading the Section Codes
The section code on each transaction tells you what kind of income the TDS relates to. It is the fastest way to spot income you forgot about.

body.caption: Section codes you are most likely to see (1961 Act numbering, used up to AY 2026-27)

cells: Interest other than on securities, such as FD interest
Fees for professional or technical services
Company hiring you as a consultant

body.text: From tax year 2026-27, the 194 series of TDS sections is consolidated into section 393 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, with numeric payment codes in place of the alphanumeric sections. The information will look different, but it answers the same question: what was paid to you, and how much tax was cut.

children.text: Booking Status Still Matters

Each transaction carries the same booking status letters you met in Form 16 Part A. F (Final) is the one you want. U (Unmatched) means the deductor's deposit did not match its statement, and O (Overbooked) means it claimed more than it paid. P (Provisional) appears for government deductors pending verification. Any status other than F is the deductor's problem to fix, but it can delay your credit.
Part II: Form 15G and 15H

If you submitted Form 15G, or Form 15H as a senior citizen, the bank does not deduct TDS. It still reports the interest paid to you, and that shows in Part II with tax deducted as zero. Part II is a reminder, not an exemption. The declaration stops TDS. It does not make the income tax-free.
Part VI: TCS Is Your Credit Too

Tax collected at source is easy to forget, because it feels like a charge added to a bill. It is not a cost. It is tax paid in advance on your behalf, and you claim it in your return exactly like TDS.

In December 2025, Priya booked a ₹2,00,000 Europe tour package with a Mumbai travel agency. For FY 2025-26, TCS on overseas tour packages was 5% on amounts up to ₹10 lakh, so the agency collected ₹10,000 on top of the package price. That ₹10,000 appears in her Part VI against the agency's TAN, and she claims it when she files.
Part VII: Refunds Paid

Part VII lists income tax refunds issued to you during the financial year, with the assessment year they relate to, the amount, the interest paid on the refund and the date of payment. In September 2025, Priya received a refund of ₹18,450 for AY 2025-26, with interest of ₹552.

body.text: The refund itself is not income, because it is your own tax coming back. The interest on the refund is income, taxable under income from other sources in the year you receive it. Priya must report the ₹552 in her FY 2025-26 return.

body.title: How was ₹552 of interest worked out?

children.text: Interest on a refund is generally 0.5% for each month or part of a month, from 1 April of the assessment year until the refund is granted, when the return was filed on time. The refund amount is rounded down to the nearest ₹100 for this purpose. No interest is paid if the refund is less than 10% of the tax determined. Priya's refund cleared that bar, since her tax for the year was about ₹1,60,000.
Where Did Advance Tax Go?

If you pay advance tax or self-assessment tax, older guides tell you to confirm it in Form 26AS. From AY 2023-24, you will not find it there. Challans for taxes you pay yourself now appear in AIS, under payment of taxes. Form 26AS on TRACES shows only TDS and TCS related data, along with refunds and defaults.

body.title: Where to confirm each type of tax paid, from AY 2023-24

columns.label: Form 26AS
points: TDS deducted by employers, banks and others
TCS collected by sellers and banks
TDS on property, rent and crypto transactions
Defaults in TDS statements you filed

columns.label: AIS
points: Interest, dividends and securities sales with no TDS

children.text: Part X: Defaults You Caused

Part X only fills up if you were the one deducting TDS. The most common case for an individual is buying a flat worth ₹50 lakh or more, where the buyer deducts 1% TDS and files the statement. If you paid late or filed with errors, Part X shows the default after processing: short payment, short deduction, interest on late payment or deduction, and late filing fees. These are amounts you owe, not credits.
Check Your Understanding

body.title: Total up Suresh's credits
body.prompt: Suresh's Form 26AS for AY 2026-27 shows: Part I, TDS of ₹92,000 from his employer and ₹4,800 from a bank; Part VI, TCS of ₹25,000 on a foreign remittance; Part VII, a refund of ₹6,000 for the previous year. What total tax credit should he claim in his FY 2025-26 return?
body.explanation: Credits are TDS plus TCS: ₹92,000 + ₹4,800 + ₹25,000 = ₹1,21,800. The ₹6,000 refund in Part VII is not a credit for this year. It is money already returned to him for an earlier year.

body.title: Selling a flat
body.question: Lakshmi sells a flat in Hyderabad for ₹80 lakh, and the buyer deducts 1% TDS. In which part of Lakshmi's Form 26AS should the ₹80,000 appear as a credit?
body.explanation: TDS on property under section 194IA appears in Part IV for the seller, who gets the credit. The buyer sees the same transaction in Part VIII as the deductor.

body.title: Spot the FD interest
body.textWithBlank: In Form 26AS up to AY 2026-27, TDS on fixed deposit interest from a bank usually carries section code ___.
body.explanation: Section 194A covers interest other than interest on securities, which includes bank FD and recurring deposit interest. Salary is 192 and dividends are 194.

body.title: Meenakshi's Part II
body.scenario: Meenakshi, 66, is a retired teacher in Chennai. She submitted Form 15H to Indian Bank, so no TDS was deducted on her FD interest. Her Form 26AS Part II shows interest of ₹2,40,000 with tax deducted as zero. Her pension is ₹4,20,000 a year. She assumes the interest is tax-free because the bank did not deduct anything.
body.prompt: Is she right? What does Part II mean for her return?
body.modelAnswer: No. Form 15H only told the bank not to deduct TDS. It does not exempt the interest. Part II is the department's record that ₹2,40,000 was paid to her. She must report it as income from other sources in her return along with her pension. Whether she owes tax depends on her regime and deductions, for example the deduction for interest available to senior citizens under the old regime, but the income must be reported either way. If her total income is above the taxable limit, she was also not eligible to submit Form 15H in the first place, and should stop doing so.

cards.definition: TDS on salary, interest, dividends, professional fees and other payments. Your main source of credit.
Interest and other payments where you submitted Form 15G or 15H, so no TDS was deducted.
TDS credit when you are the seller of property, a landlord with high rent, a professional paid by an individual or a crypto seller.
TCS collected from you, such as on foreign remittances or overseas tour packages. Claim it like TDS.
Income tax refunds paid to you during the year, with interest. The interest is taxable.
TDS you deducted yourself as a buyer, tenant or payer. A record, not a credit.
Defaults in TDS statements you filed, such as late payment or short deduction. Amounts you owe.

points: Form 26AS has ten parts from AY 2023-24, but most salaried taxpayers only need Parts I, VI and VII.
Part I shows each deductor's TAN, amount paid and TDS. Section codes tell you what the income was.
Part II entries are still taxable income. Form 15G and 15H only stop TDS.
TCS in Part VI is a tax credit you claim in your return, just like TDS.
Interest on a refund in Part VII is taxable in the year you receive it.
Advance tax and self-assessment tax no longer appear in Form 26AS. Check them in AIS.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and reflects the Form 26AS layout and FY 2025-26 rates as of September 2026. TANs and amounts shown are illustrative. For your specific situation, check the e-filing portal or consult a chartered accountant.
